items.headline: Sensex rises 1,225 points to 76,917.85 and Nifty 1.58% to 23,810.85 for a fourth straight gain
items.summary: FMCG led sectors, with private banks and financials strong. Sensex is up about 5% in four sessions after a volatile October. Rally extending on cheaper oil and foreign buying.
items.rationale: Lower crude, peace hopes and returning foreign money are lifting large caps; gains are vulnerable if Hormuz talks stall.

items.headline: Foreign investors buy a net ₹6,837 crore, a third straight day; domestic funds sell ₹3,679 crore (provisional)
items.summary: November foreign buying reaches about ₹9,952 crore after October's ₹52,100 crore outflow. Reversal gathering pace.
items.rationale: Sustained foreign inflows support large caps and the rupee; domestic funds are booking profits into the rally.

items.headline: Brent slips $1.17 to $103.60, a second daily fall, as Qatari mediators await US and Iranian replies
items.summary: Prices swung between $100.80 and $107.24 on strike headlines. Iran rejects 'diplomacy based on coercion'. Down about $14 from Friday's six-month high. Easing.
items.rationale: Crude near $104 eases India's import bill, inflation and rupee pressure compared with October.

items.headline: US carries out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian fire on US aircraft
items.summary: Target was a missile launcher; the US says it is not a return to major combat. Iran warns of stronger retaliation and says Hormuz stays shut; the US president says no talks are planned. Mixed with diplomacy.
items.rationale: Strikes near Hormuz keep a risk premium in oil and threaten the diplomacy that has pushed crude down, a key swing factor for Indian markets.

items.headline: Iranian lawmaker says ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar are exempt from Hormuz transit restrictions
items.summary: Comes as India engages the US on Hormuz security. Not confirmed by Iran's government; Iran also says the strait stays shut until the blockade ends. New, unverified.
items.rationale: If applied, exemptions could restore some Indian-bound oil and LNG flows, easing supply and freight costs.

items.headline: Democrats are projected to win both the US House and Senate in the midterms
items.summary: Networks project a Senate flip and 218 House seats. US stock futures fell on gridlock fears. New political shift.
items.rationale: A divided US government could constrain tariff and Iran-war policy, affecting India's trade terms, IT visas and oil risk; near-term effect uncertain.

items.headline: Rupee gains 13 paise to 94.71 per dollar on foreign inflows and the equity rally
items.summary: Reverses Monday's 10-paise fall. Lower oil and foreign buying support the currency. Strengthening.
items.rationale: A firmer rupee reduces imported inflation and the cost of oil, while modestly trimming exporters' rupee earnings.

items.headline: Services PMI rises to a four-month high of 55.8 in October; input cost inflation at lowest since 2020
items.summary: Below the 56.2 flash; new business grew fastest since June on domestic demand, but export orders were weakest since February 2023 and hiring eased. Composite at 56.2. Improving.
items.rationale: Strong domestic services demand and easing costs support growth and inflation outlooks; weak exports flag risk for IT and business services.

items.headline: External ministry confirms 28 Indian deaths in West Asia and Black Sea shipping attacks; 2 missing
items.summary: Up from 22 reported last week; 5 died in Black Sea attacks. Shipping lines are revamping Red Sea links to India. Escalating human cost.
items.rationale: Mounting crew deaths raise manning, insurance and freight costs for India-bound shipping and pressure policy responses.
